research.title: Evaluating interval methods for inflation forecasts
research.subtitle: Live demonstration of a master's thesis: how well do prediction intervals for monthly inflation keep their promise, and can an LLM explain them without making numbers up? Switch tabs to see the forecast, the method comparison, what the thesis found, and the explanation layer.

research.disclaimer.title: Please read: what this page is and is not
research.disclaimer.a: A thesis research prototype. It is not financial or policy advice.
research.disclaimer.b: Results are descriptive; items marked post hoc were added after other results were seen and are not confirmatory.
research.disclaimer.c: ACI is better calibrated than one-shot calibration consistently across panels; its advantage over a rolling window depends on the panel and base model.
research.disclaimer.d: DRACP versus ACI is inconclusive: the study cannot tell them apart (minimum detectable difference undefined or above 7 pp).
research.disclaimer.e: A 90% interval is not a guarantee: after shocks the real coverage can fall below 90% for a while.
research.methods.title: Three ways to calibrate an interval, tested live
research.methods.subtitle: A rolling-origin backtest for the chosen country and horizon: at every past month each method issues a 90% interval using only the outcomes already known, and we check whether the real value fell inside.
research.methods.error: Unable to run the comparison for this selection. Please try again later.
research.methods.caption: A 90% interval should contain the outcome 9 times in 10. Green dots were inside the interval, red crosses were missed.
research.methods.bandHelp: The most recent origins (down-sampled). Click a card above to switch method.
research.methods.runningHelp: Share of recent intervals that contained the outcome; the dashed line is the 90% target.
research.methods.noteWarmup: Warm-up: {{n}} revealed residuals are needed before the first interval (thesis default 48; the forecast tab uses 30).
research.methods.noteDelay: Delayed feedback: the outcome of a forecast is only known {{h}} month(s) later, so methods adapt with a lag.
research.methods.noteDescriptive: This is a single-country descriptive backtest, not a test of which method is better; see 'What we found' for the pooled evidence.
research.methods.noteWidth: Summary figures use the full history of the country (including past high-inflation periods), so mean widths are not comparable across countries.
research.findings.title: What the thesis found
research.findings.subtitle: Precomputed from the committed result files of the study (30 countries, three panels). Every number carries its evidence status.
research.findings.h1: ACI is better calibrated than one-shot (split) calibration, consistently across panels and base models (secondary contrast, no multiplicity adjustment).
research.findings.h2: ACI's advantage over a rolling window is panel-dependent: shown on one panel at one horizon, inconclusive or not shown elsewhere.
research.findings.h3: DRACP versus ACI is inconclusive: the minimum detectable difference is undefined or above 7 pp.
research.findings.ceTitle: Calibration error by method and horizon
research.findings.ceHelp: Mean over countries of |coverage - 90%|, in percentage points. Lower is better.
research.findings.contrastHelp: Difference in calibration error (negative favours the first method) with 95% block-bootstrap interval. Rule R5/E5: a minimum detectable difference that is undefined or above {{limit}} pp makes the contrast inconclusive, whatever the p value.
research.findings.contrastFoot: * Secondary contrast: unadjusted p, no power calculation, shown as descriptive. 'Inconclusive' means the study could not tell the methods apart; it does not mean they are equal.
research.findings.commoditySummary: {{n}} of {{total}} countries have commodities at 60% or more of merchandise exports (UNCTAD, 2021-2023).
research.findings.commodityFoot: Mexico, Indonesia and Georgia do not reach 60%. The classification is descriptive and was written after the panels were fixed; with so few non-qualifying countries no comparison between groups is possible (inconclusive).
research.findings.chronosHelp: Mean absolute error relative to naive B (lower is better) on clean target months only (from 2025-01), pooled over 30 countries.
research.findings.chronosFoot: Descriptive and thin (few clean months). The 2025-01 cutoff for possible pre-training leakage is an assumption.
research.findings.feedbackHelp: Coverage when outcomes arrive 12 months late (real) versus immediately (impossible diagnostic).
research.findings.feedbackFoot: Instant feedback is a diagnostic only, not a valid forecasting setup. The pre-specified 3 pp threshold of rule R4 was not met on the hold-out panel.
research.findings.nativeTitle: Conformal ACI versus native model intervals (ARIMA)
research.findings.nativeHelp: Difference in calibration error, ACI minus native. Negative means ACI is closer to 90%.
research.findings.sources: Built offline from {{n}} committed result files by scripts/thesis/build_demo_data.py.
research.explain.title: The LLM explanation layer
research.explain.subtitle: An LLM explains the calibrated forecast in English, Russian or Kazakh. In the grounded mode it may only use the numbers from the forecast service; in the ungrounded mode it has no data. Compare the two.

research.explain.sawTitle: What the model was allowed to see
research.explain.sawNone: Nothing. The model received no forecast data, so it cannot know the interval or its backtest coverage.
research.explain.trueValues: For reference, the real interval is {{lower}}% to {{upper}}% with measured coverage {{cov}}.
research.explain.checkScope: The check compares numbers only, not wording or reasoning.
research.explain.question: Question
research.explain.groundedHelp: The model receives the forecast service output and must copy its numbers.
research.explain.ungroundedHelp: The model answers from its general knowledge only.
research.explain.evalTitle: How well does this work? (one model, post hoc metrics)
research.explain.evalBody: The layer was evaluated on 936 answers from one open-weight model (13 countries x 4 horizons x 3 question types x 3 languages, 468 per condition). The corrected numeric-faithfulness metric (v2) was fixed after the pre-specified metric (v1) was seen, so both are shown.
research.explain.evalGrounded: Grounded: {{v2}} of {{n}} answers numerically faithful under the post hoc corrected metrics (v2); {{v1}} under the pre-specified metrics (v1).
research.explain.evalUngrounded: Ungrounded: {{v2}} faithful only because most contain no figures; none states a calibrated interval, since without data no interval is produced.
research.explain.evalCaveat: One model only; fluency and terminology (especially Kazakh) have not been reviewed by native speakers. The programmatic check above is a numeric filter, not a guarantee of correctness.
